newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Stena Line cites French OK for P&O deal.
newsitem.headline: Stena Line cites French OK for P&O deal.

text.p: Swedish shipping company Stena Line AB said on Monday the French government approved its plans with the Peninsular and Oriental (P&O) Steam Navigation Company about merging their cross-channel operations.
"The reasons for creating a common company with P&O on the so called Short Sea routes are overwhelming," Stena Line's chief executive Bo Lerenius said in a statement.
"This announcement is the first step on the way to establish the new P&O Stena Line."
British and European Union (EU) competition authorities also have to give their approval before the companies can go ahead with their plans, Stena Line said, adding it expected decisions shortly.
"The companies are currently discussing the merger proposal with the EU and do not expect to find it difficult to meet demands the EU could possibly make," Stena Line said.
Stena Line and P&O signed a deal at the end of last year to create a common company to compete with the channel tunnel.

The new company will be controlled equally by the companies but Stena Line will own 40 percent and P&O will hold 60 percent. The group will operate the routes Dover-Calais, Dover-Zeebrugge and Newhaven-Dieppe.

"Through merging their assets on these routes the two owners expect P&O Stena Line to make cost savings corresponding to about 75 million sterling ($122.7 million) of the company's total fixed costs of about 280 million sterling," Stena Line said.
The total assets in P&O Stena Line will amount to about 410 million sterling, the company added.
-- Birgitta Forsberg, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1017 ($ = 0.611 British Pounds Sterling)
